checked: Synonym, antonym and collocation are defined before their use. Gradable, complementary and converse meanings are given directly under Types of Opposites. Connotation, intensity, register and prefix get definitions before examples. Filipino synonym and antonym terms receive glosses. The verb in #15 is immediately explained as naming the action.

Collocation is explained through heavy rain and worked in #9. Complementarity explains eliminating one of only two allowed states and applies it in #11. Converse opposition reverses participant roles with Ana/Ben and #10. Context, strength, feeling and formality each have a mechanism and a worked application.

Complementary opposition is limited to systems with no middle state, with a stone counterexample. Gradable not-hot inference is limited in #12. Prefix advice warns that not every beginning is a prefix and requires context. Synonym substitution must preserve grammar, tone, strength and setting.
